$comment: Round 19 lane T2 (THE DENSE PAGES) - ledger-shaped entries for merge into liber-primus/LEDGER.json. Per AGENTS.md the load-bearing fields are `coverage` and `not_covered`, not `status`. Nothing here is committed by this lane; the coordinator merges.
instrument: WFA - forced alignment of canon's token sequence against the line ink (canon supplies count and order; the ink chooses the cut points), plus a leave-one-out substitution probe and deletion/insertion probes derived from the same forward/backward tables. Per-column mismatch and every DP constant are verbatim Round 9 (analysis/retranscribe/read.py); templates and the 29-class bijection are Round 9's stored artifacts. No new classifier was built - T1 owns that instrument.

entries.threshold: Registered in round19/T2/PREREG.md section 2 BEFORE measuring: gate C1 >= 0.90 loo_agreement on the LP2 pages proven by decryption; flag threshold tau fixed at the smallest value giving FPR <= 1% on those same pages, then applied unchanged elsewhere.
entries.control_detail: C1 = 1.0000 (178/178 adjudicated slots) on LP2 pages 56 and 57 - the only pages whose plaintext is known BY DECRYPTION and whose typeface is the LP2 face of pages 0-54. For comparison on the same face: round12/frontB forced re-segmentation 0.129, round19/C3 band reader 0.9556, Round 9 template DP native regime 0.980. FPR: 0 of 178 slots have delta > 0 at any threshold, so tau = 0. Second control C2' (ink-splice plant): 545 splices of a foreign glyph into real page ink, detection 1.0000 and recovery 1.0000 on all three strata - this is what rules out an inert probe. LP1 pages deliberately excluded (different typeface, outside the template domain; pooling them is what made Round 18's 44.2% and C3's 53.95% uninterpretable).
entries.result: A-01 COMPLETE. Independent per-slot agreement with canon 0.9973 over 13,121 slots on 604/604 lines (stage 2 stopped at 0.9693 over 5,207 glyphs on 232 lines). Per stratum: solved-LP2 1.0000 (178), dense pages 45-54 1.0000 (1,992), pages 0-44 0.9968 (10,951). Of 35 slot-level disagreements: 33 SEG, 0 CONF, 2 ID - and both ID cases coincide exactly with an insertion flag at the same position on a count-exact line, so both are SEG. ZERO disagreements in the corpus have the signature of a real rune-identity error in canon.
entries.coverage: 13,121 / 13,136 rune slots = 99.89%, on 604/604 canon lines and 57/57 pages. This closes Round 10's stated bound of 38.4% of lines glyph-diffable.
entries.not_covered: 15 slots, all NAMED: illuminated initials (oversized decorative first glyphs, h 497-608 px against a 113 px rune body, which no 108-120 px template can match). Also not covered: multi-rune correlated errors, transpositions, and whole-line omissions (the line map is driven by canon's line inventory, so a line canon omits entirely would not appear; the page-level count residual of 0.63% constrains but does not eliminate this).

entries.notes: Two errors found in the Round 9 write-up (doctrine R6). (1) FOUND-ERROR: retranscribe/FINDINGS.md bucket B calls LP2 pages 29/34/35 'cryptographically solved, so canon is proven correct by decryption'. They are NOT solved - LP2 pages 0-54 are the unsolved 12,956 runes. The only LP2 pages solved by decryption are 56 and 57. R9's conclusion survives (T2 reads all three at canon) but its stated reason had no ground truth behind it. (2) FOUND-ERROR: R9's bucket A, '15 loci all pinned at position 0, x=601, a mechanical DP edge effect', is diagnosed here as the illuminated initial - x=601 is its left edge, and there are 15 such line-starts. Excluding and naming those slots is what lifted T2's control from 0.9500 to 1.0000.

entries.control_detail: C1 = 1.0000 on the decryption-proven LP2 pages (frontB's forced instrument scored 0.129 and therefore certified nothing). On the dense stratum specifically: ink-splice plant detection 1.0000 and recovery 1.0000 over 189 splices; planted-canon-missing-rune localisation 0.9890 with the rune named 1.0000; planted-canon-extra-rune localisation 0.9780. The dense pages are NOT the weak stratum for this instrument - they match or beat pages 0-44 on every plant.
entries.result: SETTLED, and canon is upheld. Pages 45-54 read at 1.0000 over 1,992 slots: zero substitution disagreements (0 SEG, 0 CONF, 0 ID) and zero surviving insertion/deletion candidates. The two indel flags raised on the dense stratum both adjudicate to SEG - non-rune ink inside the band on lines whose rune-body component count matches canon exactly. Why this worked where frontB did not: frontB forced a NUMBER OF PIECES and let the cuts fall where they may; T2 forces the IDENTITY SEQUENCE and lets the ink choose the cuts, so the segmentation never has to be discovered. frontB's own reported segmentation gap (30-41 boxes per line on p45 against canon's 21-25) was an artifact of not applying its own measured height classes as a mask: with the mask, rune-component counts are exact on 530/604 lines (87.7%) against R9's 232/604 (38.4%), residual 83 glyphs over 13,136 = 0.63%.
entries.coverage: All 91 lines and all 1,992 rune slots of pages 45-54, under single-token substitution (complete, 29-way), single insertion, and single deletion.
entries.not_covered: Multi-rune correlated errors, transpositions, whole-line omissions, overlapping/kerned glyph pairs and ligatures (the transition model cannot represent them). The adjudicator's register is pixel mismatch against the R9 template library at this render; its blind spot is the shape-confusable families (U/Y, O/A/AE, L/W, C/I), which were 0 at tau = 0.

entries.hypothesis: NEW ENTRY, closing T3's stated largest gap: 'every model here is substitution-only and preserves n=12,956. Insertions/deletions and segmentation errors are not bounded at all.' How many runes can canon have inserted or deleted?
entries.objects: 13,121 deletion positions and 13,725 insertion positions over 604 lines
entries.threshold: tau_del and tau_ins set to the largest value produced by ink that is proven correct by decryption. Measured: max_del = -1860 and max_ins = -212 on LP2 pages 56/57, both strictly negative - on pages canon is proven right, canon's rune count is strictly the cheapest explanation of the ink. Both thresholds therefore fixed at 0.
entries.control_detail: Planted CANON length errors, no ink surgery: drop a token from the forced sequence (canon pretending to miss a rune the ink has) or insert one (canon pretending to carry a rune the ink lacks), one of each on every line, n = 604 each. Canon-missing-rune: fired 0.9983, localised to the right position 0.9901, rune named 0.9950. Canon-extra-rune: fired 0.9967, localised 0.9735.
entries.result: Canon can contain k <= 0.74 missing runes and k <= 0.93 extra runes at 95% confidence - i.e. k <= 1 of each - from ZERO surviving candidates over 13,121 tested positions at the measured localisation power (95% lower bounds 0.9822 and 0.9607). 26 lines raised a flag (1 extra-rune, 25 missing-rune; 0 on solved pages, 24 on pages 0-44, 2 on pages 45-54) and ALL 26 adjudicate to SEG. Crude ceiling charging every flag to canon without adjudication: <= 26 indels, all on the unsolved stream, none on a page proven by decryption. Mechanism, measured: both remaining substitution candidates and 21 of the 26 indel flags sit on a MID-SIZE MARK CLASS - ink 35-94 px tall, between a separator dot and a rune body, mostly thin vertical ticks (h ~ 50, w ~ 5-19). 487 of them across 349 of 604 lines. They appear on the decryption-proven pages too (3 on p56, 1 on p57), where canon omits them and the decrypt is correct, so the class is PROVEN NON-TEXTUAL BY DECRYPTION and canon is right not to transcribe it.
entries.coverage: Every single-token insertion at all 13,725 gap positions and every single-token deletion at all 13,121 rune slots, over 604/604 lines.
entries.not_covered: Multi-indel and correlated length errors; transpositions; whole-line omissions. Raising the band mask to rune bodies only (h >= 95) removes 20 of the 26 flags - confirming the mechanism - but BREAKS the control (1.0000 -> 0.9775), because the same 35-94 px class also contains genuine split strokes of real runes. No single height threshold zeroes both; that is a real limit of component-height stripping at this render, and the operating point chosen is the one whose control is exact.
entries.reproduce: cd liber-primus/analysis/round19/T2 && python3 indel.py && python3 score_indel.py && python3 adj_indel.py && python3 orphan.py && python3 variant.py
entries.reopens_if: The 35-94 px mark class (out_orphan.json, 487 marks) is shown to carry information - a separate question from transcription fidelity, which this lane did not test. Or a second LP2-face solved page disagrees.
entries.notes: Why this matters more than the substitution bound: T3 measured that the DECODE channel is the fragile one (at k=200 substitutions 17% of correct-key decodes derail, at k=450 50%, and max_skip can only run the key ahead, never recover sync). An indel breaks sync outright, so the indel curve is far steeper than the substitution curve. T2's result is that the INPUT to that curve is 0, bounded at <= 1. The steepness is real but there is nothing to feed it. What would strengthen this is NOT a higher DPI - at 2400x3600 the median glyph already has a pixel-identical twin, and the residual is class ambiguity in the 35-94 px band, not resolution - but the publisher's vector/font source.

entries.result: ALL 19 LINES READ. Canon is correct on every one, in count AND in position. The Round 8 diffs are its own instrument, in two distinct failure modes: 10/19 are a line-alignment slip (Round 8's dot count for the image row equals canon's separator count at a NEARBY canon line, d in -4..+4; its count-based DP aligned 599 of 604 lines where T2's mask-based map aligns 604/604), and 9/19 are a dot-extraction failure - four of them (glines 536, 538, 545, 550, all on dense pages 47-48) Round 8 measured at ZERO dots, where cropping gline 545 shows six separator dots plainly, exactly matching canon's six '-'. Root cause of the whole shortlist: Round 8 counted EVERY component with h < 30 as one separator dot, but the mark classes are cleanly bimodal - a word separator '-' is ONE dot spanning 9-10 px (2,767 of them) while a sentence mark '.' is a LOZENGE spanning 24-60 px that fragments into 3/4/10/13/23 components (187 of them). A single '.' therefore contributed up to 23 to Round 8's count. This independently confirms round18/L4's fitted advance widths ('.' 1.82 against '-' 0.32).
entries.coverage: All 19 shortlisted lines, and the whole-book audit behind them: 604/604 lines. Canon 2,764 '-' and 183 '.'; image 2,767 '-' and 187 '.'. Lines with exact separator counts 582/604 (96.36%); with exact separator POSITIONS 580/604 (96.03%).

This lane did not attempt to re-attribute separators across line boundaries.

cross_lane.T1: T1 owns the per-glyph classifier and the 450 O/A/AE adjudication; T2 did not touch either and built no second classifier. The instruments are complementary: T1 needs the connected components to be right (its segcheck reports -95 over LP2, mostly merges), while T2 takes the count from canon and is therefore immune to merges. T2's CONF column (0 at tau = 0) is the natural place to cross-check T1's confusion matrix.
cross_lane.T3: T2 supplies the numbers T3's propagation curves need, in T3's requested form. Substitutions: 0 confirmed, crude ceiling 2 (pages 4 and 40), both on the unsolved stream - two orders of magnitude below T3's k = 200 first-derailment point. Insertions/deletions: 0 confirmed, bounded at k <= 1 at 95% confidence, crude ceiling 26 (24 on pages 0-44, 2 on pages 45-54), all on the unsolved stream, none on a page proven by decryption. This closes the gap T3 named as its largest.
cross_lane.C3: T2 reuses C3's identification of the solved-page renders (73.jpg = LP2 p56, 74.jpg = LP2 p57 at 2400x3600) and follows C3's warning to report LP1 and LP2 separately - LP1 is excluded from every T2 control as outside the template domain. T2's control (1.0000) is above the 0.9556 at which C3's own reader errs, which is the bar T3 set for any claim about canon.
cross_lane.R1: T2 is itself a closure audit in R1's sense: the two FOUND-ERRORs in section 4.2 of RESULTS.md come from auditing Round 9's write-up rather than from any new search.
